subject: Post-demo streaming SLOs & pilot milestones

Subject: Post-demo streaming SLOs & pilot milestones

Hi Beth / Helix team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-demo recap so we have alignment on the performance/operational items we covered and clear next steps for the pilot kickoff. I grouped things into SLOs, open clarifications, and immediate MAP items.

1) Proposed SLOs (inference surface unless noted):
- Latency: p99 <= 200 ms (inference server-side, streaming chunks measured as time to first partial + tail)
- Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec for your peak batch (90th percentile of our sample traffic)
- Concurrency: support for 30 concurrent sessions with KV cache reuse across requests
- Streaming: chunk interval <= 150ms for small updates (short responses), support for chunked token streaming without rebuffering under load

2) Clarifications we need from Helix:
- Confirm whether the latency SLO should be p99 inference-only vs p95 end-to-end (client + network).
- Typical sequence length distribution (mean, 90th pct) and token budget per response.
- Any strict bandwidth/MTU limits on your side for streaming chunks.

3) Immediate MAP (owners & targets):
- Pilot kickoff call (align measurement plan & canary): owner Logan — propose Mon 2028-04-17
- Share traffic sample & authentication details (Helix) — owner Beth — action: send sample by EOD Thu 2028-04-13
- Redwood to provide instrumented test harness and SLO checklist (attachment) — owner Soojin — delivery: EOD Fri 2028-04-14
- Pilot run plan and load target config (attachment: pilot-MAP) — owner Marissa / Dylan — delivery: Mon 2028-04-17

Attachments: [Attachment: SLO-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)]

If the high-level SLOs above look OK, can you confirm (a) p99 inference-only acceptance, or (b) different end-to-end target, and (c) whether the 2-week pilot window works for Helix?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up to lock the schedule.

— Logan

Subject: Re: Post-demo streaming SLOs & pilot milestones

Thanks Logan — great demo. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: we prefer p95 end-to-end <= 250ms for client-facing SLAs, but we understand the value of separating inference-only p99 for technical acceptance. For the pilot let's set two gates: inference p99 <= 200ms (technical) and e2e p95 <= 250ms (product).
- Pilot duration: 2 weeks of steady-state traffic plus two stress windows (one with 2x peak load).
- Sequence length: average 40 tokens, 95th pct around 180 tokens. Typical responses are short-ish incremental updates (our streaming UI updates every ~120ms currently).
- Security/compliance: we'll need a short note on data retention for pilot logs (can you confirm logs are retained 30 days by default and can be configured?)

Attached is a small traffic sample and a redacted request/response trace for your test harness.

Attachment: [Helix_traffic_sample_20280411.json (redacted, 18KB)]

I can target EOD Thu 4/13 to send full access details for the test environment. Happy to take the pilot kickoff on Mon 4/17 — 10am PT works for our team.

Best,
Beth

Hey Beth / team —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — helpful. A few technical confirmations and a short list of knobs we recommend to reliably hit the inference p99 <= 200ms target on Redwood: 

- Model & runtime: we recommend a quantized rLARGE variant with KV caching enabled; our internal benchmarks at your median sequence length (~40 tokens) show p99 inference ~140–170ms on the dedicated instance profile we demoed.
- Streaming behavior: to match your UI cadence (~120ms updates) we'll stream tokens with small chunk sizes (4–8 tokens) and enable continuous batching with a max hold of 20ms to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Concurrency & throughput: to sustain 120 req/s with concurrency 30 we recommend pre-warmed pool with autoscale burst up to 50 slots for the 2x stress window.

Open items we need from Helix to finalize configuration: 
- Confirm whether the 95th/99th percentiles should exclude back-end network time (we can measure both server-only and e2e).
- Provide any TLS termination specifics or gateway rate-limiting that might affect observed client latency.

Attached is the initial pilot MAP we discussed — it specifies test harness steps, metric collection points (server inference p50/p95/p99, e2e p50/p95), and rollback criteria.

Attachment: [Attachment: pilot-MAP-v1.pdf (12 pages)]

Proposed next steps (owners & ETA):
- Soojin: deliver instrumented test harness and baseline run (Thu 4/14)
- Marissa/Dylan: configuration for canary + fallback rules (Mon 4/17)
- Beth: provide access + traffic sample (Thu 4/13)

If these align I’ll schedule a short 30m technical sync immediately before the kickoff to walk the team through the harness and measurement dashboards.

— Soojin

Quick operational notes from my side: 

- Measurement: we'll provide a per-request token-level breakdown and a streaming trace so you can see first-byte and tail timings. Dashboards will show inference-only and e2e aggregates side-by-side.
- Canary & fallback: recommended canary (5% traffic) for 24 hours, then 25% for 48 hours. Fallback policy: automatic fallback to smaller model variant if p99 inference crosses 250ms for >5 minutes.
- Cost/throughput trade-offs: we expect slightly higher unit cost for the low-latency config (smaller hold windows / smaller batch sizes). We will provide a cost estimate with the pilot run results.

Drive link to test harness and dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pilot-harness

Happy to review the pilot-MAP on the kickoff call.

— Marissa

- Pilot start: Mon 2028-04-17, 10:00 AM PT (kickoff & measurement alignment).
